headline: Reduced and extended ODE models resolve glycolytic and circadian clock dynamics
label: Dynamical Models Of Cellular Processes
summary: Recent preprints pair explicit dynamical formulations of cellular processes with open-source tooling for simulation and analysis.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the specification of cellular processes as explicit dynamical systems, with states, rates, and perturbations defined so that behavior can be simulated, probed, and tested. The glycolysis preprint derives a reduced two-dimensional Othmer-Aldridge-type ODE for oscillations from a multiscale stochastic Markov chain model, linking stochastic and deterministic descriptions. The plant circadian clock study extends an ODE model with added regulatory modules and applies sensitivity, phase portrait, knockout, and network-index analyses to identify key mechanisms and essential interactions. What is new here is the release of BSTModelKit.jl, an open-source Julia package for constructing, solving, and analyzing S-system power-law models of biochemical networks. The modalities differ, so the shared element is methodological rather than a single biological finding.
